meta.titre: Prepositions: dependent prepositions and fixed phrases
meta.sous_theme: Choosing the correct preposition in gap-fill sentences

source.epreuve_titre: GCE A/L English Language past paper (Cameroon)

sections.contenu_markdown: A shopkeeper in Douala puts up a notice: "Closed on Sundays. Open from eight in the morning until five in the evening." Every small word in that notice tells you something exact about time. Prepositions are small, but a wrong one changes the meaning or makes the sentence incorrect. GCE gap-fill items test them often, especially the pairs that cannot be guessed from meaning, such as congratulate on or depend on.

items: A noun names a thing, a pronoun replaces a noun, and an -ing form is a verb ending in -ing used as a noun or after a preposition.
A phrase is a group of words without its own subject and verb.
A cause answers the question why, and a contrast shows something unexpected.

sections.contenu_markdown:
### What a preposition does

A preposition links a noun, a pronoun or an -ing form to the rest of the sentence. It shows place, time, direction, cause or another relationship: *in the room*, *after lunch*, *because of the rain*. What follows a preposition is a noun, a pronoun or an -ing form, never the base verb: *She is good at drawing.*

### Dependent prepositions

Many verbs, adjectives and nouns need one particular preposition. Learn them as pairs, not as separate words.

| Type | Pairs |
|---|---|
| Verb + preposition | congratulate (someone) on, apologise to (a person) for (a fault), accuse (someone) of, blame (someone) for, prevent (someone) from, suffer from, succeed in, believe in, rely on, depend on, consist of, complain about, wait for, listen to, laugh at |
| Adjective + preposition | good at, interested in, afraid of, fond of, proud of, responsible for, capable of, aware of, keen on, tired of, married to, different from, similar to, satisfied with, worried about, famous for |
| Noun + preposition | reason for, cause of, increase in, demand for, solution to, need for |

### Preposition followed by -ing

In some expressions the word *to* is a preposition, so the verb after it takes -ing: *look forward to*, *be used to*, *object to*, *with a view to*. Compare *I want to go* (infinitive) with *I look forward to going* (preposition + -ing). Other prepositions work the same way: *instead of walking*, *without asking*, *after leaving*.

### Cause and contrast

*Because of*, *owing to*, *due to* and *on account of* introduce a cause and are followed by a noun phrase or an -ing form: *The road was blocked because of a fallen tree.* *Despite* and *in spite of* introduce a contrast: *Despite the noise, he slept.* Note that *despite* is never followed by *of*.

### Time and place

| Word | Use | Examples |
|---|---|---|
| at | exact time, point | at noon, at the gate, at night |
| in | months, years, parts of the day, enclosed space | in July, in 2019, in the evening, in the room |
| on | days, dates, surfaces | on Friday, on 5 May, on the table |
| for | length of time | for three weeks |
| since | starting point of time | since 2016 |
| during | within a period | during the holidays |
| by | not later than | by Friday |
| until | up to a time | until Friday |
| between / among | two / more than two | between the two houses, among the pupils |

variantes.quand_utiliser: When one preposition is missing after a verb, an adjective or a noun
variantes.contenu_markdown: Read the word before the gap and recall the whole phrase. Usually the word before the gap, and not the general meaning of the sentence, decides the preposition. Learn pairs in groups: *apologise to ... for*, *accuse ... of*, *prevent ... from*. If two prepositions seem possible, think of a person after the verb (agree with a person) or a plan (agree to a plan).

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the gap is followed by a verb with -ing, or by a fixed expression
variantes.contenu_markdown: Ask whether the gap word is a preposition. If it is, the verb that follows takes -ing. *With a view to* is followed by a noun or an -ing form: *with a view to buying land*. *Look forward to*, *be used to* and *object to* work in the same way.

variantes.quand_utiliser: When the gap is followed by a noun phrase of reason, time or position
variantes.contenu_markdown: For a reason, choose among *because of*, *owing to*, *due to* and *on account of*. For a contrast, use *despite* or *in spite of*. For time, think: point (*at*), period (*in*), day (*on*), length (*for*), starting point (*since*), deadline (*by*).

sections.enonce_markdown:
Complete the sentence with the correct prepositions.

*The company was fined ______ polluting the river, and its manager apologised ______ the villagers ______ the damage.*

etapes.action: Mark each gap and the words around it.
etapes.justification: There are three gaps: after *fined*, after *apologised*, and after *villagers*.
etapes.resultat_markdown: fined ___ polluting / apologised ___ the villagers / ___ the damage

etapes.action: Decide what follows the first gap.
etapes.justification: *Polluting* is an -ing form, which is possible after a preposition. The verb *fined* takes *for* to give the reason.
Someone who apologises says sorry to a person. The person here is *the villagers*.
The thing the manager is sorry about is *the damage*. The pair is *apologise to (a person) for (a fault)*.
All three gaps make the sentence grammatical and keep the meaning.

sections.conclusion_markdown: The completed sentence is: *The company was fined **for** polluting the river, and its manager apologised **to** the villagers **for** the damage.*

items.erreur_markdown: *I look forward to see you soon.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: In *look forward to*, the word *to* is a preposition, so the verb must take -ing.
items.correction_markdown: Write **I look forward to seeing you soon.**

items.erreur_markdown: *Despite of the rain, the match continued.* (wrong)
items.pourquoi_faux: *Despite* is never followed by *of*. Only the longer form *in spite of* contains *of*.
items.correction_markdown: Write **Despite the rain, the match continued** or **In spite of the rain, the match continued.**

items.pourquoi_faux: The adjective *good* takes *at* when it means skilled at a subject or an activity.
The verb *discuss* already carries the meaning of *talk about*, so it takes no preposition.

items.enonce_markdown:
Fill each gap with one preposition.

(a) The children are afraid ______ the dark.

(b) She is very good ______ mathematics.

(c) We are waiting ______ the bus.

(d) He depends ______ his uncle for school fees.

Fill each gap with a preposition of time or place.

(a) The meeting starts ______ nine o'clock.

(b) She was born ______ a Tuesday.

(c) The prize was shared ______ the three finalists.

(d) We have lived here ______ 2015.

(e) It rained ______ the night.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **at** (exact time)

(b) **on** (a day)

(c) **among** (more than two people)

(d) **since** (starting point)

(e) **during** (within the period of the night)

items.enonce_markdown:
Fill each gap with the preposition or prepositions that fit. Give a reason for each answer.

(a) She is looking forward ______ meeting her cousin.

(b) The match was postponed ______ the heavy rain.

(c) He is married ______ a nurse.

(d) The match continued ______ the rain.

(e) The nurse succeeded ______ calming the frightened child.
items.solution_markdown:
(a) **to**. In *look forward to*, the word *to* is a preposition, so *meeting* has -ing.

(b) **because of** (or **owing to**). A cause is introduced by a cause preposition.

(c) **to** (married to).

(d) **despite** or **in spite of**. The rain would normally stop a match, so the sentence shows a contrast.

(e) **in** (succeed in), followed by the -ing form *calming*.

items_markdown: A preposition is followed by a noun, a pronoun or an -ing form, never the base verb.
Learn dependent prepositions as whole pairs: good at, afraid of, depend on, apologise to ... for.
In look forward to, object to, be used to and with a view to, the word to is a preposition, so the verb takes -ing.
Because of, owing to and due to introduce a cause; despite and in spite of introduce a contrast, and despite takes no of.
Use at for exact time, on for days and dates, in for months, years and parts of the day, since for a starting point and for for a length of time.
